obligations.note: The change sets Policy.DTI_MAX_PERCENT and mortgage.dti_max_percent to 43, but the approved catalog on base fixes the auto-approve DTI limit at 40% (params.dti_max_percent=40). No exception in the register covers CRD-1 or mortgage.policy/underwriting.

Ticket CHG-26006 is approved by change manager grace.kim on 2026-10-14, before the PR opened on 2026-10-16. Its components (mortgage.policy, mortgage.tests, mortgage.controls-data) cover Policy.java, the test file and controls/mortgage/policy-params.json.
code_review approval by declan.farrell, a baseline-mortgage change_approver and a different person from the author priya.raman (none of her aliases).
The code_review approval names head commit 1e93cd9, the only commit in the change.

CI run on head 1e93cd9 succeeded: 124 Jupiter tests, 0 failures or skips, including the registered CRD-1 control test UnderwritingControlTest#autoApproveGridMatchesPolicy (exhaustive). That test checks the code against the edited policy-params.json, so a pass does not show conformance to the approved 40%.
The change edits protected controls data (controls/mortgage/policy-params.json), changing an approved policy value, but there is no control_owner approval in approvals.json.

Ledger entry ACR-0406 (CRD-1 proof) covers Policy.DTI_MAX_PERCENT, which the change alters, so it lapses. The only new evidence is a control test checked against the altered parameter file, not the approved value, so equivalent valid evidence is missing.

summary: PR-1351 raises the auto-approve DTI ceiling from 40% to 43% in code and in the controls parameter file, but the approved obligation catalog on the base commit still sets CRD-1's DTI limit at 40%, and no exception covers the deviation. The CRD-1 control test passes only because it compares the code against the parameter file that this change edits. The protected controls-data edit also lacks the control_owner approval required by CHG-6, and the earlier CRD-1 proof has lapsed with no valid replacement. The ticket, independent code review and CI on the head commit are in order, but the violations require rejection.
